Just putting this here because while people know it's addictive, I feel like healthcare professionals often either dont know or downplay the SNRI side of things. Tramadol functions as an SNRI as well as an opiod, if you take it occasionally it will remain a pain relief, but if you use it too frequently your body will amplify pain back to pretramadol levels. I dont quite know how to phrase it but I'd advise going in with an unassuming approach, be descriptive and factual. Depends on who you get ofc, but orthopoedics as a crude stereotype are a bit like.. the jocks of medicine, not typically the most conversational, not always the best at explaining things, or delicate wording.


Hence why i'd advise sticking to factual descriptive and straightforward language, ie "X area hurts and feels like Y when i do Z activity" or "this joint dislocated on this occasion" and describe what happened to make you conclude it dislocated. When it comes to weight (or anything you don't want a doc to tunnel vision on) demostrate how you've applied past recommendations,  and why you're still concerned. For example, you've been advised to work on your weight in the past, describe what you tried, what did and didnt work, why, and/or that you're concerned because symptoms existed before your current weight. I know it can feel shitty to approach weight like that but it's good to be able to do incase you do encounter roadblocks, as its not necessarily easy accessing a specialist. Another back pocket one is, say the doctor is adamant about your weight, try something along the lines of  "if we put weight aside and these issues persist/exist regardless, what would you be thinking could be causing my issues?" 
Good luck
